text: There once was a stonecutter who wished to be great
A lord passed him by in his silk and his state
Oh, if I were him, he sighed at the gate
And so it was, by the turn of fate
But the sun beat down on the lord all day
Then let me be the sun, he heard himself say
He burned as the sun and the earth turned dry
Till a cloud rolled over and covered the sky
Then let me be the cloud, was his cry
He rained and he rained till the rivers ran wide
But one thing stood still on the mountainside
Let me be the mountain, he cried
Now mighty, unmoving, he stood in his pride
Then he felt a tap, tap, tap at his feet
A stonecutter's chisel, steady and neat
Let me be myself, he whispered, complete
Whatever you become, something stands greater still
Peace begins with who you are, and always will
